description: Pinned source versions for UniPad experiments (PRD 8.1 inputs). Every run must be reproducible from this file plus the recorded hashes.

device_repo.commit_note: Pinned 2026-10-31 (sixth revision). A fork of xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu at the previous pin 89fc5a0267066a5d49a4911df4f0c0b34dfc5d91 plus exactly one commit, which builds the display hand-off's userspace client -- the ring the 2026-10-30 measurement located but could not close. MEASURED then: native_qemu_metal_opens=1 with the owners slot decoding to b'back' (QemuMetalPublish.cpp:50's prediction, confirmed), and native_gop_gpu_offers=0 with the device open and rendering. NativeGOPPresenter::offer() says why: it accepts an offer only while a privileged client is inside waitSwap(), which is the only place gpuClient is set, and that client did not exist -- bridgephase::serveScanout is started by NativeAdrenoMetalPlugin.mm and was started by nothing here. So the GPU path was one-sided, and no counter could tell 'no client' from 'a client that was refused'. This commit supplies both halves, reusing upstream's shared pieces (GpuScanoutClient.h, GpuScanoutPresenter.h, NativeGOPWire.h and the presenter's own entry points) rather than writing a second copy: the kernel gains a second open type 0x4148 for a connection that serves only the hand-off and takes no slot of the window, and QemuMetalScanout.mm opens that connection inside backboardd, probes for a selector the sandbox admits, and serves frames on its own thread. It probes rather than assuming selector 0x7000 for the reason upstream's Adreno plugin does: which selectors a profile lists is decided outside the process. The bundle's CDHash is EXPECTED TO CHANGE (a new source is linked into it), and then the payload step refuses naming board.toml's trust_cache_sha256 -- a visible re-pin, not a silent one. Status: CODE COMPLETE, compile UNVERIFIED on the Windows code-stage host (no toolchain), Windows real acceptance UNVERIFIED. Pinned 2026-10-31 (fifth revision). A fork of xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu at the previous pin b52eb29cc4c31d78caed48dd08c888f29d438d7c plus exactly one commit, which PINS the QemuMetal owner trust cache at 2a4b737e1fd2fc073678c9ccf4cf71de00d2ce77c001ce0ea702bea00041ded0. MEASURED: run 41132638822 reproduced run 41125151494 exactly -- the same CDHash 6080ce8fac2b57b2fdd1046663bb536a2d2996ab and the same derived cache digest. The cache is a pure function of the CDHash, so a matching cache digest is a byte-level confirmation rather than a second opinion about the same hash. Two runs WITHOUT -Wl,-no_uuid disagreed (a1fce7f8... and 68518f18...); two runs WITH it agree. The previous revision of this note recorded LC_UUID as refuted on one data point with the flag, which was wrong, and board.toml now carries all four runs so the next reader does not repeat it. The digest is still expected to change when the bundle's sources do, and then the payload step refuses naming board.toml's list -- a visible re-pin rather than a silent one. Pinned 2026-10-31 (fourth revision). A fork of xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu at the previous pin cc7e8db08b6a9f3ef783ae4e5f7af3245ca39c07 plus exactly one commit, which REMOVES the owner trust cache digest the previous revision had pinned and probes why the bundle's CDHash moves. MEASURED: run 41108366328 built the bundle at CDHash a1fce7f8870b9ea068add82ddaa4bfd5b1343aad with owner-trust.bundle at 665af2ff7440ec1404522c7e2ddbf45e733d7e7261d452d2ebe9ed341da6351a; run 41117052708 built the SAME sources with the SAME flags on the SAME toolchain at CDHash 68518f18395a53dac252b52b2481902af17faa0c with owner-trust.bundle at b646229b20c7f08e41ce2fe62c8fc01ed39e3abf6d7e9afabec672d6bfbff737. The only difference between the two pins is board.toml itself. So the bundle's build is NOT reproducible, and the payload step refused a cache that is correct -- naming the allowlist this fork had just extended. A digest known to move is worse than no digest: it makes 'the bundle changed' read as 'the board is wrong' on every run. Nothing in the repository has been shown to vary (no __DATE__/__TIME__/arc4random/gettimeofday in package/QemuMetal or drivers/NativeMetal; the include paths are one tree at one pinned commit), so the remaining candidate is ld64's per-link LC_UUID, which lands in the first page and is therefore inside the ad-hoc signature's hashed range; this commit adds -Wl,-no_uuid to test that. The comment in build-qemu-metal.py states in those words that it is a hypothesis and not a shown fix. Either outcome is informative: two runs with the same CDHash prove reproducibility and the digest can be pinned again; two runs with different CDHashes refute this and name the next candidate. Pinned 2026-10-31 (third revision). A fork of xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu at the previous pin 0f1a0834d9e17b455446495c429aab45e21999df plus exactly one commit, which adds the QemuMetal owner trust cache to [payload] trust_cache_sha256. MEASURED on run 41108366328: with the two bridge stubs supplied, build-qemu-metal.py guest succeeded for the first time and produced QemuMetal.bundle (CDHash a1fce7f8870b9ea068add82ddaa4bfd5b1343aad), owner-trust.bundle (sha256 665af2ff7440ec1404522c7e2ddbf45e733d7e7261d452d2ebe9ed341da6351a) and owner-data-1g-metal.dbr (1 GiB seed, packed to 4,772,048 bytes). The second build then picked up BOTH the owner trust cache and the Metal Data seed -- the preference the workflow was given works -- and the payload step refused with '.../build/qemu-metal/owner-trust.bundle is not one of the trust caches this board accepts (board.toml [payload] trust_cache_sha256)'. That refusal is the allowlist doing its job, and the new entry is required for the same reason build-qemu-metal.py trust() exists: the own module carries the bundle's CDHash, and without an owner module AMFI runs launchd but refuses the plugin -- so the original cache alone cannot boot a guest where the Metal device is openable. The digest is EXPECTED TO CHANGE whenever the bundle does (the own module is a pure function of the CDHash), so a rebuilt bundle lands as a refusal naming this list, which is a visible re-pin rather than a silent one. Pinned 2026-10-31 (second revision). A fork of xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu at the previous pin a88fc1a454fe1dd230242deb8cb98ccf5944d516 plus exactly one commit, which supplies the two nmb_* functions QemuMetalRemote.cpp was missing. MEASURED on run 41099656091, the first run that ever executed build-qemu-metal.py guest: the link of QemuMetal.bundle/QemuMetal fails with 'Undefined symbols for architecture arm64' for _nmb_buffer_new_no_copy_releasing (referenced from -[NBDeviceMethods newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:...] and surfaceBuffer(__IOSurface*, void*, unsigned long)) and _nmb_texture_new_on_surface (referenced from textureOnSurface(NBBuffer*, MTLTextureDescriptor*, ...)). Every other nmb_* symbol the frontend uses is already supplied by QemuMetalRemote.cpp, which is this board's stand-in for the Rust bridge -- so this was an omission, not a design change. nmb_buffer_new_no_copy_releasing is nmb_buffer_new_no_copy plus Metal's deallocator, so NmbBuffer gains the two fields it needs and nmb_buffer_release runs the deallocator while buffer->guest still names the caller's pages; a refused call never sets them, which is the contract NativeMetalObjects.h:66-68 states. nmb_texture_new_on_surface routes through textureOnBuffer with surface=true, because the wire struct has no field for the plane set (QemuMetalWire.h:105 carries descriptor, offset, bytesPerRow, bytesPerImage and surface): what this board can tell the Mac is 'these bytes are a surface', and which plane or where plane 1 sits cannot be sent, so those six parameters are read and dropped rather than guessed at. Plane 0 of a one-plane surface -- every surface this guest makes today -- is described exactly. This is also the first evidence that the QemuMetal userspace half can build at all: before this commit nothing in the repository ran build-qemu-metal.py guest, so the plugin bundle never existed and native_qemu_metal_opens could not leave 0. Pinned 2026-10-29. A fork of xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu at the previous pin 5c0770d3074c9827be943edbd6ab0a8fabb11ac1 (itself a comment correction) plus exactly one commit, which raises [payload] kernel_args' offline-legacy-surface-wait-ms from its 120000 default to 600000. MEASURED over ten boots of one matched build on the Windows host: four reached native_legacy_stage=10 and six stopped at stage 8, the give-up path, and in all six native_legacy_surface_status was 0 (the IOSurface kext loaded) with surface_found=0 -- so waitForMatchingService("IOCoreSurfaceRoot") timed out rather than the kext being absent. With 600000 the same build reached stage 10 on both of the next two boots, with surface_found=1, unit_scale_calls=1, chosen_scale=1, native_gop_ready=1, and native_gpu_addon_stage=1 / status=2 (the addon mount attempted and refused ENOENT, as previously recorded). The wait is on its own thread -- what this fork's first commit bought -- so a longer value costs only time on a boot that would fail anyway, while a boot that loses the display silently is the expensive kind; the 120 s default was calibrated for a boot whose mountroot completed at t=49.6 s and whose surface landed at t=63.6 s, and the stalled boots are roughly twice as slow throughout. NOTE the three commits before this one on this fork are comment corrections recording a measurement error: a four-boot 'control' was taken to refute the claim that sheng-fb-gpu=1 constructs the presenter, but unipad's stage_esp() regenerates unixnu.toml from board.toml when BootInputs.payload_toml is None, so the payload image's own args are never read and all four boots carried sheng-fb-gpu=1 from here; the original conclusion stands. Platform seed moves cce5d68284272b42 -> the value derived from this commit; verify_adt's leading-zero comparison defect is already fixed. Upstream is read-only for this account; the fork is public and carries no private material. Re-pin to upstream as soon as the change is accepted there.

feeds_note: The union of TWO feeds.toml files, not one: UniXNU/feeds.toml and the device repository's UniXNU-qemu/feeds.toml (which 'adds to' UniXNU's and may override a ref). dyld comes from the device repository alone and IOStorageFamily's ref is the device's override. A lock derived from UniXNU's feeds.toml by itself is missing dyld -- that is exactly the gap this note exists to prevent, found by cross-checking `unixnu status` against this array on 2026-10-24 (8 of 9 agreed; dyld was absent here). Re-derive with `unixnu status -D <device>` and compare every `refer` line.
frozen_note: Not frozen, and the reason is the BUILD, not the compiler. tools.clang IS proven to cross-compile AArch64/iOS on this host (three independent lines of evidence, see tools.clang.note); what is missing is a clean XNU build run against these pins, which needs six build blockers cleared (docs/kernel-build-windows.md) and two required XNU patches applied to the build tree (kits/NativePrelink/patches/xnu-10063.141.1-sparse-index.patch and -security-init.patch, both currently UNAPPLIED). The firmware layer IS verified on the host (see tools.firmware_boot). Set frozen=true only after a clean XNU build succeeds against these pins. pinned_checkouts_note: Three repositories are pinned here, and only two of them are in `feeds`. `unixnu` and `device_repo` are the two the driver cannot clone for itself (cli.py has no subcommand that clones either; scripts/unixnu/config.py raises 'no device repository' without -D), so the workflow's acquisition step clones them into vendor/. `uefi_sheng` is NOT a feed on purpose: the driver's feeds.fetch() resolves sources named by a feeds.toml and writes them into out/<board>/feeds, and uefi-sheng is named by no feeds.toml -- it is the Mu-Silicium checkout the driver's --uefi option points at (cli.py:24). Adding it to `feeds` would make the workflow's cross-check demand it in the driver's own unixnu.lock, where it will never appear, and would fail every run. So it is pinned here, acquired by the same step, and verified by the one file the build actually reads (uefi_sheng.font_header.sha256) rather than by a feed pin. Measured 2026-10-25: with it absent, build-payload failed on run 40094234507 and 40096928333 with 'Font.h is missing'.

submodules.commit_note: MOVED BACK one commit from UniXNU's own gitlink, deliberately and on evidence. Measured on run 40187668943 (stage M4): build-os-root.py reached step 9 for the first time -- storage-abi, both signed policies, the verified-root probe, NativeVirtioBlock/NativeRamBlock verified bindings, the grown 1 GiB OwnerData volume (675761EF-5622-4F5B-89DF-4CAD5BA456F6) and the packed ramdisk all passed -- and then died in build-native-legacy-display.py -> build-arm-driver.py NativeLegacyDisplay with `NativeLegacyDisplay.cpp:206:59: error: only virtual member functions can be marked 'override'` and `:207:13: error: no member named 'getRefreshAttributes' in 'IOMobileFramebufferLegacy'`. The pinned device repository (xVanTuring/UniXNU-qemu 97b75b1f, its only branch, at its tip) generates OriginalLegacyFramebufferABI.h from a fixed slot table that has no entry for slot 301, and its own invariant then refuses the override: `require(i in (0,1,7,14,84,86,87,141,155,184,188,288,290,296) or i in pure, 'Only qualified own methods and guarded leaves override')`. So the device repository is incompatible with c031d882 and with everything after it, and there is no newer device commit to move to. c031d882 is `feat(display): report the panel refresh rate`; eb9c949 is its parent `fix(gop): re-kick the swap queue after each retirement`, whose override set is exactly the one the device repository's generator declares. What is given up is the sheng-vsync refresh-rate report, which is gated on a boot argument this board does not pass and affects no root-mount or launchd path (PRD/Goal 6: the display is not a gate for them). gitlink_commit records what UniXNU b881ac7d actually pins so the divergence is auditable rather than silent; build-macos.yml forces the assembled tree's checkout to `commit` before it runs the chain.

clang.note: Present on this host as a HOST compiler (x86_64-w64-windows-gnu) AND PROVEN to cross-compile AArch64/iOS. Three independent lines of evidence, all re-run on this host: (1) clang -target arm64-apple-ios17.0 -c emits real Mach-O arm64 objects whose disassembly shows genuine AArch64 instructions, and ld64.lld links a real Mach-O arm64 executable (docs/implementation-plan.md fact 4); (2) docs/kernel-build-windows.md records 61 of 123 osfmk/kern translation units compiled to genuine Mach-O 64-bit arm64 objects, including the 138 KB / 174-symbol osfmk/kern/bsd_kern.c; (3) an 80-line shim plus three -D rewrites for the Apple-clang-only builtins takes that to 79 of 123 with zero regressions. CORRECTION to an earlier note here, which said 'NOT yet proven to cross-compile AArch64/iOS: no iOS sysroot' -- that conflated two different facts. There is indeed no iOS sysroot, and that is still true; but cross-compiling to a Mach-O arm64 object does not require one when the headers are supplied, which is exactly what the freestanding header shim does. The claim of 'not proven' was wrong. What is NOT done is a clean XNU BUILD against these pins -- six build blockers remain (iig, csh/doconf, the five SETUP host tools, ditto/python3 wiring, the Darwin freestanding header set, the Apple-clang builtins; docs/kernel-build-windows.md has the detail), and two required XNU patches are still unapplied in the build tree. availability.pl is present and runs under the host Python (907 lines / 292 macros emitted), so it is not a blocker. mig IS built and working (bootstrap_cmds-138, 73/73 kernel MIG outputs); unifdef and mtools are present in the MSYS2 tree.

uefi_sheng.commit_note: Pinned 2026-10-25 at the tip of the default branch `sheng` (tarball UniXNU-uefi-sheng-v4.0-52-g20ac23d). The third pinned checkout: NOT a feed and NOT part of either repository above. board.toml [payload] panic_screen = true (UniXNU-qemu/board.toml:94) makes `unixnu build payload` run the device repository's patch-xnu-entry-probe.py --panic-screen, which compiles scripts/xnu-panic-screen.c; that file's ONLY include is "Font.h" (xnu-panic-screen.c:294) and patch-xnu-entry-probe.py:183 takes it from (UNIXNU_UEFI or <tree>/uefi-sheng)/Silicon/Silicium/SiliciumPkg/Library/FrameBufferSerialPortLib. The assembled build tree never contains uefi-sheng/ (tree.py:assemble creates only drivers/ kits/ patches/ refer/ build/ .cache/ package/ scripts/), so without this pin the payload stage died in clang with "fatal error: 'Font.h' file not found" -- measured on run 40094234507.

unixnu.commit_note: Pinned 2026-10-30 (third revision). A fork of UniXNU/UniXNU on fork branch unipad/gpu-addon-ngpu-dir, whose SHA was read back from api.github.com/repos/James081105/UniXNU/commits/unipad/gpu-addon-ngpu-dir and equals the local commit. It is the previous pin 0b7612913cd7546503d818733210eff417ad8571 (itself a fork of 2a97d2dba51b65774b54a4a7e930fd51896602a5, itself a fork of ab3199c90b13478c80fbfb7242f1d56a3c3bae83, which is a fork of upstream b881ac7dc1695ce676c856873051a487c6a9f963 plus one commit moving native_legacy_display_late_probe() to just after IOSecureBSDRoot) plus one commit fixing the SECOND hunk header the first two left behind. The chain: (1) zzy-native-gpu-addon-mount.patch's native_gpu_addon_parents() scanned for '/' starting at sizeof("/private/var/ngpu/") - 1 = 18, the index AFTER the trailing slash, so its first mkdir was /private/var/ngpu/addons and every mkdir below a nonexistent parent failed ENOENT -- measured 2026-10-30 on bundle8 (run 40955285309's build) as native_gpu_addon_files=10, native_gpu_addon_failed=10, native_gpu_addon_error=2, with all three bindfs mounts failing their first vnode_lookup with the same ENOENT. /private/var/ngpu is not an iOS directory, so it is in neither the OS image's /private/var nor the Data seed, and provision-data-seed.py deliberately does not add it -- make-gpu-addon.py's own docstring says "The kernel creates missing directories" and the seed's content hash is its identity, so this project's mount point cannot come from the seed. (2) That fix grew a comment by thirteen lines and kept hunk 1's count at 321, so git apply refused the patch as corrupt at build-xnu-4k-baseline.sh:44 on run 40971549320 -- after the whole owner root chain had run. (3) Correcting hunk 1's count to 334 shifts every later hunk in the same file, and hunk 2's new-side start was still 7566 where it is now reachable as 7579; run 40981242194 failed on exactly that, at the same line 44. A hunk header carries THREE numbers, not two: the counts and the start. Checks (2) and (3) are now tests/unit/test_pinned_patches_apply.py plus scripts/shared/check_patch_hunks.py, which validates counts AND that consecutive hunks are reachable by the same gap on both sides. Upstream is read-only for this account, so the fix cannot be delivered there; the fork is public and carries no private material. Re-pin to upstream as soon as the change is accepted there.
